title: Adversarial verification of self-reported 100/100 audits (sample of already-audited stories)
headline: None of the five 100/100 audits is defensible. Every story has at least one AC whose observable behaviour is implemented only as a pure-function return value (or a caller-supplied flag) with no assertion on the postcondition the AC names. The IAM and Knowledge domains have no product consumer at all (0 imports outside their own tests), so '0 writes', '1 bản ghi từ chối', 'risk entry', 'flow fixed' postconditions cannot be satisfied, only echoed back.

per_story: picked the 3 ACs with the strongest behavioural claims (state change / refusal / record)
read the implementing source and every test that names the AC id
ran the suites (node --test) to confirm green, then ran out-of-band probes under /tmp/eso-dd/*.mjs to test behaviour the tests do not cover
test_runs: green tests are necessary but were treated as insufficient; every PASS below is backed by reading the assertion, not by the run
probes: /tmp/eso-dd/probe1.mjs — declaration resolution order-dependence with duplicate ids
/tmp/eso-dd/probe4.mjs — concurrent handover + duplicate worker id without existingWorkers

sampled.claim: override wins across zones and records overridden_by path@version list
code_evidence: eso/knowledge/src/resolver.mjs:265 — const projectItem = candidates.find((c) => c.zone === 'project' || c.project === project);
eso/knowledge/src/resolver.mjs:298 — if (sharedItem) overriddenList.push(formatPointer(sharedItem));
sampled.note: Assertion is on the observable result (winner zone + overridden_by contents), not on input shape. Accepted. Minor: formatPointer defaults a missing version to '1.0' (resolver.mjs:258), so an unversioned lower-zone declaration is recorded as @1.0 — a fabricated pointer the AC never authorises.

sampled.claim: agent modifying applies_when is rejected AND recorded, with 0 changes, error RULE_CHANGE_FORBIDDEN
code_evidence: eso/knowledge/src/guard.mjs:9 — export function guardDeclarationWrite({ actor_role, declaration, changes } = {}) {
eso/knowledge/src/author.mjs:188 — export function saveDeclaration({ declaration, previousDeclaration, projectConfig = {}, declarations = [] } = {}) {  (no actor_role parameter, no guard call)

MISSING: any non-test caller of guardDeclarationWrite — grep -rn 'guardDeclarationWrite|RULE_CHANGE_FORBIDDEN' over eso/ qc/ excluding test files returns only eso/knowledge/src/guard.mjs itself and the index re-export
test_evidence: qc/eso-kb-why.test.mjs:84 — test('SCN-KB-07 (AC-KB-02-04): Agent modifying applies_when is rejected with RULE_CHANGE_FORBIDDEN (0 changes)' — calls guardDeclarationWrite in isolation only
eso/knowledge/test/knowledge.test.mjs:400 — same isolated call pattern, plus allowed=true for operator
sampled.proof_of_gap: Probe /tmp/eso-dd/probe2.mjs: saveDeclaration({declaration:{...applies_when:{always:true}, version:'1.1'}, previousDeclaration:{applies_when:{paths:['**/*.ts']}}}) returned 'saved: true applies_when: {"always":true} warnings: 0'. An agent can rewrite applies_when through the only real write path; the guard is an unwired orphan.
sampled.note: Also unimplemented: the AC's '+ ghi' (record the refusal). guard.mjs throws and returns; nothing is persisted or emitted. Audit rated this PASS.

sampled.claim: ED3 — deterministic result; same input => same order; 0 dependency on file order (10 000 declarations)
code_evidence: eso/knowledge/src/resolver.mjs:265 — const projectItem = candidates.find((c) => c.zone === 'project' || c.project === project);  (first-in-array wins inside a zone; no version tie-break)
eso/knowledge/src/resolver.mjs:307 — resolved.sort((a, b) => ...)  (sorts output by id only, after the winner has already been chosen by array position)
test_evidence: eso/knowledge/test/knowledge.test.mjs:448 — it('AC-KB-02-06 / ED3: 1000 declarations resolution is deterministic regardless of array order') — 1000 unique ids (AC says 10 000), reversal of distinct ids

qc/eso-kb-why.test.mjs:122 — test('SCN-KB-22 (AC-KB-02-06 & AC-KB-02-07): Deterministic sorting and unmasking shared version upon override removal') — asserts only res1[0].from / res1[0].version; no sorting and no order permutation is exercised despite the name
sampled.proof_of_gap: Probe /tmp/eso-dd/probe1.mjs: two project-scope declarations of the same id (v1.0 and v2.0) resolve to v1.0 for declarations:[v1,v2] and to v2.0 for declarations:[v2,v1] -> 'deterministic: false'. AC-KB-02-06 explicitly demands 0 dependency on file order.
sampled.note: Distinct-id sorting is deterministic; same-id multi-declaration election is not. No test covers it, and the test claiming to ('Deterministic sorting') asserts nothing about ordering.

evidence: equivalent (not named by the AC): qc/eso-kb-why.test.mjs, eso/knowledge/test/knowledge.test.mjs
ac_section3_tests.impact: Equivalent tests carrying the AC ids exist, so this is not by itself a FAIL; but the AC's declared proof surface is gone and neither the audit nor any artifact records the substitution.

story_defects.proof: eso/knowledge/src/author.mjs:188 saveDeclaration has no actor param; probe2 saved applies_when {always:true} as an agent with 0 warnings

story_defects.title: Determinism breaks on duplicate ids inside one zone
story_defects.proof: eso/knowledge/src/resolver.mjs:265 find() by array position; probe1 order A -> 1.0, order B -> 2.0

story_defects.title: AC-KB-02-06 asks for 10 000 declarations; the test uses 1000

audit_claim.details: 'orphaned work routed to OPEN risks with owner + review_by'

sampled.claim: retiring a worker with unfinished work -> work becomes OPEN risk WITH owner + review_by; work is not lost
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/worker.mjs:78 — export function retireWorker({ worker, activeWork = [], reviewer = 'operator' } = {}) {  (pure function, no db, no store)
eso/iam/src/worker.mjs:96 — owner: work.new_owner || work.owner || null,
eso/iam/src/worker.mjs:97 — review_by: reviewer,
MISSING: call to eso/evidence/src/risk.mjs:24 openRisk(db, {...}) from retireWorker — the risk register is never written
sampled.proof_of_gap: The assertion list at qc/eso-iam-retire.test.mjs:31-34 checks status, review_by, task_id, project — it never asserts `owner`, which is the half of the AC the audit claims ('OPEN risks with owner + review_by'). And `review_by` is set to an actor name, while the design says it is a date: sdlc/07.technical/01.architecture/03.v2-high-level-design.md:943 — review_by : ngày.
sampled.note: AC §3 explicitly asks the test to prove 'đĩa/DB không mất việc' (work not lost on disk/DB). There is no disk/DB: the test inspects a returned array. The audit called this 'dedicated test coverage'.

sampled.claim: unknown role is rejected with UNKNOWN_ROLE and 0 workers created
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/worker.mjs:60 — if (catalogRoles && Array.isArray(catalogRoles)) { ... UNKNOWN_ROLE
sampled.note: Rejection is real and asserted. '0 workers created' is vacuous because nothing is ever created — acceptable here because the negative branch is the observable.

sampled.claim: ED6 — creating a worker with an existing id halts with DUPLICATE_ID; only 1 worker exists
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/worker.mjs:22 — existingWorkers = [],
eso/iam/src/worker.mjs:40 — const duplicate = existingWorkers.find(...)
test_evidence: qc/eso-iam-duplicate-id.test.mjs:18 — existingWorkers: existing,  (the test hands the prior state in)
sampled.proof_of_gap: Probe /tmp/eso-dd/probe4.mjs: createWorker({project:'p', worker_id:'dup', role:'build'}) twice with no existingWorkers list -> both calls return worker_id 'dup', no throw. Duplicate detection depends entirely on the caller supplying the registry that does not exist.
sampled.note: The assertion is real but only proves the guard works when the caller volunteers the evidence. AC says 'tạo lại -> DUPLICATE_ID'.

story_defects.title: Audit claims owner is asserted for orphaned OPEN risks; no test asserts owner
story_defects.proof: qc/eso-iam-retire.test.mjs:31-34 asserts status/review_by/task_id/project only; eso/iam/src/worker.mjs:96 owner defaults to null

story_defects.title: review_by carries an actor name instead of a date
story_defects.proof: eso/iam/src/worker.mjs:97 review_by: reviewer; test pins 'operator-lead' (qc/eso-iam-retire.test.mjs:32) vs sdlc/07.technical/01.architecture/03.v2-high-level-design.md:943 — review_by : ngày

story_defects.title: Orphaned work never reaches the evidence risk register
story_defects.proof: eso/evidence/src/risk.mjs:24 openRisk(db, {...}) has no caller in eso/iam; retireWorker returns an in-memory array

sampled.claim: two roles with different bar judging the same work yield different levels, differing exactly on the bar-caused part; both judgments recorded with role
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/role.mjs:119 — export function evaluateRoleSufficiency({ role, evidence = [] } = {}) {
eso/iam/src/role.mjs:161 — level: isSufficient ? 'SUFFICIENT' : 'INSUFFICIENT',
MISSING: any caller of evaluateRoleSufficiency outside tests — grep 'evaluateRoleSufficiency' over eso/ returns role.mjs + index export only; no judgement/verdict engine consumes it
sampled.note: The bar genuinely changes the answer and the deficit is pinned to the right evidence kind — good. But the AC asks for two *judgments* on the same work recorded with their role ('hai phán quyết ghi kèm role'), and AC §2 allows 'mức thấp hơn hoặc cannot-judge'. What exists is a standalone two-valued sufficiency helper with no judgment record and no consumer; the 'level' scale has no cannot-judge arm.

sampled.claim: agent attempting to change a worker's role is refused AND the refusal is recorded (1 bản ghi từ chối), 0 change, ROLE_CHANGE_FORBIDDEN
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/role.mjs:93 — export function changeWorkerRole({ worker, newRole, actor = 'operator' } = {}) {
eso/iam/src/role.mjs:104 — const err = new Error(`ROLE_CHANGE_FORBIDDEN: Actor '${actor}' cannot change worker role ...`);
MISSING: refusal record — nothing is written or emitted on the refusal branch (role.mjs:104-108)
sampled.note: 'Không đổi' is genuinely asserted (line 29). '1 bản ghi từ chối' is neither implemented nor asserted; the audit's ac_coverage lists this AC as PASS without qualification.

sampled.claim: agent role with empty bar is refused with EMPTY_OBLIGATION, 0 roles saved
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/role.mjs:55 — const err = new Error(`EMPTY_OBLIGATION: Agent role '${name}' cannot have empty bar obligations ...`);
sampled.note: Both the code and the message assertion are real. One asymmetry: role_type defaults to 'agent', so an operator role created without role_type is silently subject to agent rules — not covered by the AC.

story_defects.title: Audit PASS on AC-IAM-02-04 while the refusal record it names does not exist
story_defects.proof: eso/iam/src/role.mjs:104 throws only; qc/eso-iam-role-rbac.test.mjs asserts err.code and worker.role_name, never a refusal record

story_defects.title: Bar-driven 'level' is a standalone helper with no consumer and no cannot-judge arm

audit_claim.ac_coverage: 7/7 PASS, 'matching exact error codes and combining logic'

sampled.claim: allow + deny both match -> deny wins; both matched laws and the deciding law are recorded
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/policy.mjs:146 — const denyPolicy = matched.find((p) => p.effect === 'deny');
sampled.note: Real combining behaviour with both laws returned and the decider named — matches the AC. Fail-closed default (no match => deny) also verified by probe3.

sampled.claim: agent changing a law is refused on BOTH routes (direct and via delegation), 1 refusal record stating which route
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/policy.mjs:37 — const isAuthorized = actor === 'operator' || actor === 'human' || actor === 'A-01';
eso/iam/src/policy.mjs:39 — const err = new Error(`POLICY_CHANGE_FORBIDDEN: Actor '${actor}' cannot change policy (${channel})`);
MISSING: delegation mechanism — savePolicy takes `channel` as a caller-supplied string (policy.mjs:16 default 'direct'); the code never detects an indirect route
test_evidence: qc/eso-iam-policy-indirect.test.mjs:38 — channel: 'indirect',  (value written by the test, then asserted back at :51 assert.equal(err.channel, 'indirect'))
sampled.note: The 'indirect' half of AC §2 is a label the test passes in, not a blocked second route — there is no agent-to-agent delegation surface in the product at all. '1 bản ghi từ chối' is unimplemented (throw only). AC §2 warns explicitly: 'Nếu chỉ kiểm đường trực tiếp, hệ trông an toàn mà vẫn hở.'

sampled.claim: a project outside its authority calling ANY endpoint gets 403 OUT_OF_SCOPE — same wording as a non-existent project
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/policy.mjs:81 — if (target.project && project && target.project !== project) {

MISSING: HTTP/403 surface — no route, no status code in eso/iam; the domain is never imported by eso/control-plane, eso/core or packages/* (grep for 'eso/iam' / '@mu/eso-iam' outside its own tests: 0 hits)
sampled.proof_of_gap: Probe /tmp/eso-dd/probe3.mjs: evaluatePolicies({project:'proj-allowed', target:{stage:'prod'}}) does not throw — 'no throw; effect= deny reason= NO_MATCHING_POLICY'. A caller whose target carries no project field is indistinguishable from an in-scope caller.
sampled.note: No 403, no 'same sentence as a project that does not exist' comparison (no existence oracle at all). The code checks a cross-tenant attribute mismatch, which is AC-IAM-03-04's territory.

story_defects.title: Indirect policy-change route is simulated by a caller-supplied label
AC-IAM-03-07 has no endpoint and no existence-indistinguishable 403
story_defects.proof: eso/iam/src/policy.mjs:81 only fires when target.project is present and different; probe3 shows no throw otherwise

story_defects.title: No refusal record for POLICY_CHANGE_FORBIDDEN although the AC postcondition demands one

sampled.claim: worker with work + a receiver retires: handover recorded, work changes owner, worker inactive
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/handover.mjs:12 — export function handoverWorkerWork({ worker, activeWork = [], recipient, allowOpenRisk = false, reviewer = 'operator' } = {}) {
eso/iam/src/handover.mjs:68 — state: 'retired',  (AC text says worker `inactive`)
sampled.note: Ownership transfer and the handover record are genuinely asserted — the strongest of the five stories. Gaps: nothing is persisted ('ghi bàn giao' is a returned object), and the resulting state is 'retired' while AC-IAM-07-01 says `inactive` and AC-IAM-01-02 says `retired` — the SoT contradicts itself and the worker CHECK constraint only allows 'retired' (eso/iam/src/schema.mjs:41).

sampled.claim: a retired worker still referenced in a flow is surfaced AND the flow is either fixed or an OPEN risk is opened; postcondition 0 flow pointing at a retired worker
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/handover.mjs:128 — if (dangling.length > 0) {
eso/iam/src/handover.mjs:131 — code: 'DANGLING_FLOW',
MISSING: any remediation — checkFlowDanglingWorkers mutates nothing and opens no risk; the flow still references the retired worker after the call
sampled.note: Diagnostic half is implemented and asserted; the 'sửa hoặc OPEN' half and the postcondition '0 flow trỏ người đã nghỉ' are absent. Under the strict baseline this is a data shape standing in for the state change the AC demands — but because the surfacing half is real and visible, PARTIAL rather than FAIL.

sampled.claim: ED7 — retiring DURING an in-flight handover yields exactly one handover, work not lost, 1 new owner
code_evidence: eso/iam/src/handover.mjs:28 — if (worker.state === 'retired' || worker.state === 'inactive') {  (the only guards are on the caller's snapshot)
MISSING: lock, version check or atomic claim — no CAS/transaction anywhere in handover.mjs
test_evidence: qc/eso-iam-retire-race.test.mjs:38 — workerState = firstResult;  (the 'race' is two sequential calls, the second fed the first one's output)
qc/eso-iam-retire-race.test.mjs:40 — assert.throws(() => handoverWorkerWork({ worker: workerState, ... }), ALREADY_INACTIVE)
sampled.proof_of_gap: Probe /tmp/eso-dd/probe4.mjs: two handovers from the SAME stale snapshot both succeed — 'A state/owner: retired r-A' / 'B state/owner: retired r-B' -> 'both succeeded (no single winner): true'. That is exactly the ED7 case the AC names.
sampled.note: The test proves sequential re-entry, not concurrency; the AC says 'nghỉ trong lúc bàn giao đang chạy'. The audit scored this AC PASS and cited 'disjoint slices'.

story_defects.title: ED7 concurrency is untested and unimplemented — two stale-snapshot retires both win
story_defects.proof: probe4: both handoverWorkerWork calls return state 'retired' with owners r-A and r-B; qc/eso-iam-retire-race.test.mjs:38 feeds the first result into the second call

story_defects.title: DANGLING_FLOW is surfaced but never remediated; postcondition '0 flow trỏ người đã nghỉ' is false
story_defects.proof: eso/iam/src/handover.mjs:128-134 returns a diagnostic object; no mutation, no risk

story_defects.title: State vocabulary conflict: IAM-07 says `inactive`, IAM-01 says `retired`, schema allows only 'retired'
story_defects.proof: sdlc/.../45.iam-us-07-retire.md §1 vs 05.iam-us-01-workers.md:AC-IAM-01-02 vs eso/iam/src/schema.mjs:41 CHECK (state IN ('declared','active','paused','retired'))

cluster_defects.title: All five audits are non-defensible: self-reported 100/100 with 0 findings while named postconditions are unasserted
cluster_defects.proof: ESO-130 AC-02-04 (guard unwired), ESO-176 AC-01-02 (owner unasserted), ESO-181 AC-02-04 (refusal record absent), ESO-186 AC-03-02 (refusal record + fake indirect route), ESO-315 AC-07-05 (race not tested). Each audit file lists the AC as PASS with findings: [] — e.g. comments/artifacts/slp/audit/ESO-186-audit.json:22 — "AC-IAM-03-02": "PASS"
cluster_defects.impact: The audit gate (>=85 & 0 CRITICAL) was passed by artifact, not by inspection. Any downstream 'Human In Review' sign-off resting on these scores is unsupported.

cluster_defects.title: eso/iam is an island: no consumer anywhere in the product
cluster_defects.proof: grep -rnE "from '.*iam/(src|index)" over eso/ packages/ qc/ excluding qc/eso-iam-* and eso/iam/* returns 0 hits; the same holds for eso/knowledge
cluster_defects.impact: Every IAM AC whose expected behaviour is a state change on a user-visible object (worker row, risk entry, refusal record, flow rewrite, 403) can only be a returned object. The audits never note this.

cluster_defects.title: Guard-style ACs are satisfied by an unwired function that the real write path bypasses
cluster_defects.proof: eso/knowledge/src/author.mjs:188 saveDeclaration has no actor parameter; probe2 saved applies_when {always:true} as an agent (saved: true, warnings: 0)
cluster_defects.impact: AC-KB-02-04 and AC-IAM-03-02 are RBAC invariants (INV-KB-02). A bypassable guard is worse than no guard because the tests certify it.

cluster_defects.title: Tests named after a property that they do not assert
cluster_defects.proof: qc/eso-kb-why.test.mjs:122 — test('SCN-KB-22 (AC-KB-02-06 & AC-KB-02-07): Deterministic sorting ...') asserts only res1[0].from / version; qc/eso-iam-retire-race.test.mjs:9 — 'Concurrent retirement ... exactly one winner' performs two sequential calls
cluster_defects.impact: The audit read test names as coverage. Name-based coverage inflated 5 ACs to PASS.

cluster_defects.title: AC-KB-02 §3 test surface is 4/4 missing and the substitution is undocumented
cluster_defects.proof: MISSING: qc/eso-kb-select.test.mjs / qc/eso-kb-select-nomatch.test.mjs / qc/eso-kb-override.test.mjs / qc/eso-kb-select-rbac.test.mjs — none exist; equivalents live in qc/eso-kb-why.test.mjs
cluster_defects.impact: Not a FAIL (equivalents exist and carry AC ids), but the SoT's proof pointers are dead and no artifact records it.

notes: Sampling was the strongest-behaviour 3 per story as instructed; pass/partial/fail counts in the summary are over the sampled ACs, not the file totals (7/5/7/7/5).
Green suites do not discriminate: all 68 relevant tests pass. Every defect above was found by reading assertions and by probing behaviour the tests omit.
Not re-verified as defects (timestamps may explain them): stale test counts in ESO-176 ('5 pass / 6 pass') and ESO-181 ('12 / 13') versus the current 24 and 25.
